_comment: ROYAL AMBULANCE COLOR TOKENS v1.0. Machine-readable mirror of snippets/palette.css, for generators that cannot parse CSS: python-pptx, python-docx, matplotlib, reportlab, weasyprint pipelines. Color only. Type values are NOT duplicated here; read snippets/type-tokens.json for the family, weights, scale, leading, tracking and measure.

palette._comment: Raw brand palette. CSS name --royal-<key>. Purple is the whole palette.

purple.use: workhorse accent. Column headers, accent bars, callout borders, label chips, buttons, links, brand-colored text on white.

darkPurple.use: dominant brand color. Header bands, hero backgrounds, section dividers, table header fill.

lightPurple.use: tertiary accents and hover only. Never a large background. Never text on white.

royalPurple.use: logo fill on light. Alternate dark accent. Action or highlight nodes in flowcharts.

white.use: page background. Text on any dark purple ground.

muted.use: secondary and tertiary text, captions, footer left rail, unit labels.

hairline.use: table rules, card borders, footer top border.

surface.use: very light purple tint. Alternating table rows, callout fills.

semantic._comment: Identical NAMES in every brand. A component written for one brand renders correctly in another with only palette.css swapped. Style through this layer. Reach for a raw palette value only where the brand color is the point.

fgOnDark1.use: primary text on a dark ground

fgOnDark2.use: body text on a dark ground

fgOnDark3.use: captions and eyebrows on a dark ground

borderBandRule.use: Royal has no accent rule under the band. Apex does.

status._comment: Identical in every brand so an operational signal never changes meaning between documents. A brand accent is never a status color.

diagramRoles._comment: Identical in every brand so a diagram reads the same regardless of whose document it sits in. Rectangles, 6px radius. Role is communicated by fill, never by shape. Never invent a new hue for a role. Each role names the text color that clears contrast on its own fill; measured, do not substitute.

decision.textRule: large or bold only, which is what a node label is. Never body copy on this fill.

warning.textRule: near-black, not white. White on this amber measures 2.70:1 and fails at every size.

action.use: Royal action or highlight node. Royal only. Not in brands.json and not in the other kits

shape.rule: rectangles, 6px radius. Role is communicated by fill color, never by shape.

data._comment: HOUSE DATA COLOR v1.0. Identical in every kit and never forked. Mirrors snippets/data-color.css. A brand accent is never a series color; slot 1 is the one sanctioned exception and Royal maps it to Royal Purple. Verify any set with scripts/validate-palette.py. Reasoning and measured numbers in reference/data-color.md.

series._comment: Categorical identity. Assign IN ORDER, never cycle, never generate a ninth. The order is the color-blindness safety mechanism. Worst neighboring pair: dE 9.8 simulated red-green and 22.3 normal vision on light, 14.5 and 26.4 on a dark ground. Cap of 3 on scatter, bubble, map and small multiples. Amber and orange sit below 3:1 on white and need a direct label or a table.

sequential._comment: Magnitude. One hue, light to dark, landing on Royal Purple at step 700. Steps 100 and 200 are for continuous scales only. Discrete ordered marks start at step 300. On a dark ground the anchor flips: the lightest step means the largest value.

diverging._comment: Polarity, distance above or below a baseline. Poles are red and teal, NOT red and green: red against green measures dE 5.5 under simulated deuteranopia and collapses into one color. The midpoint is gray on purpose, because a hue there reads as a value rather than as no difference.

direction._comment: Is this good news. Color follows favorable against unfavorable. It NEVER follows the arithmetic sign of the delta and never the direction of the arrow: a cost falling and transports rising are both favorable. Every value ships with an arrow or icon AND a word. The ink step is for text on the matching tint fill.

caution.note: Replaces --status-warn #B5821A for anything read as text. #B5821A measures 3.40:1 on white and was never legal at body size.

comparison._comment: The before-and-after chart, which is the most common chart in Royal material. Two tints of the brand hue is the defect this layer exists to fix: they are too close to separate, so the reader has to read the labels. An inert gray baseline against the accent reads instantly.

baseline.use: the prior period. Inert, and nothing to feel about it

comparison.variant: On a single-metric hero slide the result bar may take the direction color instead. One slide, not a deck: if every bar is green, green stops carrying information.

chrome._comment: Recessive by policy. The grid is a hint, never a feature.

logos._comment: Ask for a ROLE, never a filename. `-on-light` is the version you place ON a light background. `-on-dark` goes ON a dark one.

logoSpec.clearSpace: padding on all four sides equal to the height of the crown mark
logoSpec.recolor: never. Pick the file for the ground.

shadow.policy: The house is flat. Shadow signals elevation, never decoration.
